_readme: Copy this to main.parameters.json and fill in the four starred values below.
main.parameters.json is gitignored — it names your machine and your admin
addresses, which is not information a public repository should carry.
Every other parameter has a working default. See the @description on each
one in main.bicep for what it does before you change it.

_comment: ★ REQUIRED. The PUBLIC half of an SSH key pair — the contents of a .pub
file, starting with 'ssh-ed25519' or 'ssh-rsa'. Never the private half.
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/librechat -C librechat-admin
cat ~/.ssh/librechat.pub
This is the break-glass account. Day to day, sign in with your Entra ID
identity instead — `az ssh vm -g <rg> -n <vm>` — which needs no key file
and can be revoked centrally. This key is what gets you back in when
that path is broken.
★ REQUIRED. The only addresses allowed to reach SSH. Everything else is
refused by the network firewall before it reaches the machine.
curl -fsS https://api.ipify.org
⚠️  Home broadband addresses change without warning, and when yours does
you are locked out. That is recoverable and takes about a minute — Azure
Portal > nsg-librechat-prod > allow-ssh-admin > edit the source. Read
docs/troubleshooting.md#locked-out-of-ssh now rather than while it is
happening.
Listing an office range and your home address is reasonable. Listing
0.0.0.0/0 defeats the purpose of the rule.
★ REQUIRED. Where every monitoring alert is sent, including the one that
fires when the site is down. A shared mailbox someone reads beats an
individual's address that goes quiet during annual leave.
★ Set this once DNS points at the machine. It is the check that notices
the application is broken while the machine itself looks perfectly
healthy — a crash-looping container uses no CPU and no memory, and every
other alert stays green through it.
Leave it as an empty string for the first deployment, then set it and
redeploy the template. Nothing else needs to change.
https://chat.example.org/health
Names every resource: vm-librechat-prod, nsg-librechat-prod, and so on.
The key vault and storage account additionally get a short uniqueness suffix,
because their names must be unique across all of Azure, not just your
subscription. Read the real names from the deployment outputs.
3 to 11 characters.
Pick the region closest to your users. If you are subject to data
residency requirements, this is the parameter that satisfies them.
az account list-locations --query "[].name" -o tsv
The VM, its public address and its data disk must all be in the same
zone or they cannot be attached to each other. Not every region offers
every zone.
4 vCPU / 16 GB runs the whole stack comfortably for a few hundred users.
Standard_D2s_v3 (2/8) works for a small pilot and costs about half.
docs/cost-model.md has real numbers.
Resizing later is a reboot, not a rebuild — the data disk is a separate
resource and comes with you.
Databases, uploaded files, letterheads and local backups all live here.
128 GB is generous for a few hundred users. Growing a disk later is easy;
shrinking one is not, so do not oversize speculatively.

adminUsername._comment: Local administrator account on the virtual machine.

_comment: The repository this machine deploys from. Change it to your fork if you
have one. It must be PUBLIC — the machine has no git credentials, and
that is deliberate: it is the reason autodeploy needs no configuration.
Daily whole-machine backup with 30-day retention. This is the only thing
that restores uploaded files. Turn it off only if you have deliberately
arranged something else.
The five-minute timer that pulls and deploys new commits. Leave it true
for a zero-configuration setup.
Set false where a pipeline triggers deploys instead, so that a timer run
cannot race a pipeline run. Maryland Legal Aid sets false and deploys
through GitHub Actions.
